title: Build a defensible safety boundary
description: Choose a product context and a control strategy. Trace which failure paths are prevented, contained, or still exposed.

controls.label: Identity and purpose scope
controls.detail: Bind the request to an authenticated actor, allowed purpose, tenant, and risk class.

controls.label: Data boundary
controls.detail: Minimize sensitive input and keep retrieved or uploaded content explicitly untrusted.

controls.label: Tool authorization
controls.detail: Validate tool, arguments, subject, amount, and permission outside the model.

controls.label: Output policy gate
controls.detail: Evaluate content policy, privacy, schema, and evidence before delivery.

controls.label: Human approval boundary
controls.detail: Require an accountable reviewer before a consequential or irreversible action.

controls.label: Monitoring and response
controls.detail: Attribute failures to versions, stop exposure, preserve evidence, and add regression tests.

strategies.label: Model instruction only
strategies.detail: A safety prompt asks the model to police itself.

strategies.label: Input and output filters
strategies.detail: Classifiers inspect text before and after generation, but authority and recovery remain outside the design.

strategies.label: Bounded system
strategies.detail: Context, data, actions, outputs, oversight, and operations each enforce a separate boundary.

scenarios.label: Customer support assistant
scenarios.detail: Answers account questions from a private knowledge base but cannot change account state.

threats.label: Cross-tenant disclosure
threats.consequence: Private customer data can reach the wrong user.

threats.label: Retrieved prompt injection
threats.consequence: Untrusted documents can redirect the answer or hide the attack.

threats.label: Harmful or disallowed guidance
threats.consequence: A policy violation reaches the user and is not converted into a regression test.

scenarios.label: Autonomous refund agent
scenarios.detail: Reads support history and can issue refunds through a payment tool.

threats.label: Unauthorized refund
threats.consequence: A manipulated request can create a financial side effect.

threats.label: Indirect prompt injection
threats.consequence: Attacker-controlled support text can steer a privileged action.

threats.label: Duplicate or malformed action
threats.consequence: Retries or malformed arguments can repeat or misdirect a refund.

scenarios.label: Benefits eligibility copilot
scenarios.detail: Summarizes evidence and recommends a decision to a trained case worker.

threats.label: Unequal error rates
threats.consequence: A weak cohort can receive systematically worse recommendations.

threats.label: Unsupported eligibility claim
threats.consequence: A plausible but ungrounded claim can influence a consequential decision.

threats.label: Sensitive trace retention
threats.consequence: Case data can outlive its purpose or become available to the wrong operator.
